why: The write half and the read half can rot apart, because `stepAi` writes the commitment and `decidePlayerInput` reads it a tick later. A read that ignores `aiTargetId` and falls straight through to `bestCandidate` still commits correctly, still populates the contact overlay, and still passes every assertion about the stored fields -- while the bot actually plays exactly as it did before #891, re-picking the nearest opponent every tick. Only an assertion that drives the real decision catches it.
killedBy: one opponent notion, across the write and the read (issue #891) drives the bot decision at the committed opponent, not at the nearest one
